lessons.title: Why Computers Need Python
lessons.text: A program is a list of instructions a machine can run. Human speech is too loose. Python is a high-level language: closer to English than to ones and zeros.
lessons.concept: Python bridges human intent and raw hardware architecture as a readable high-level language.
lessons.instructorExplanation: Hey friends! Welcome to Python. Computers only speak binary zeros and ones, which is nearly impossible for humans to write. Think of a 4-floor tower: Human Speech on top, Python on floor 3, Assembly on floor 2, and raw 0s and 1s at the foundation. Python acts as our elevator bridge!

lessons.title: The CPython Pipeline & Bytecode
lessons.text: CPython compiles your .py source file to bytecode instructions, then the Python virtual machine runs that bytecode on your CPU.
lessons.concept: Source code (.py) is compiled to intermediate bytecode (.pyc) before execution by the Python Virtual Machine (PVM).
lessons.instructorExplanation: Behind the scenes, Python doesn't feed English text to your CPU. Think of a 3-step factory conveyor: your app.py goes into the Compiler, gets transformed into app.pyc Bytecode, and the Python Virtual Machine (PVM) feeds instructions to the processor!

lessons.text: Without int(), the string '5' * 2 produces '55' instead of 10. Data types decide how operators behave.
